description.value: The study investigated cognitive regulation of negative emotion and related brain activation and subjective experience in unmedicated depression.

spans.text: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) was used to examine cognitive regulation of negative emotion in unmedicated Major Depressive Disorder (MDD).

value: The primary hypothesis was that depressed participants would not be able to cognitively increase or reduce their negative emotional responses, as measured by valence ratings and brain activation.
Weaker modulation of brain activation by reappraisal was expected in the MDD group.

description.value: Participants viewed negative pictures after the PHOTO cue and were instructed to imagine that the scenes were old, posed photographs being viewed from a distance, thereby increasing psychological distance and dampening negative responses.

spans.text: Thus, in response to the photo cue, participants were told to imagine that scenes were old, posed photographs being viewed from a distance.

Trials included a cue word (“REAL”, “LOOK”, or “PHOTO”; duration: 1 s), a jittered inter-stimulus interval (ISI: 3-5 s), a negative or neutral picture (6 s), a second ISI (1.5-3 s), and a rating screen (3 s).
The task was programmed in E-Prime (Psychology Software Tools, Inc; Sharpsburg, PA).

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to mentally place themselves in real scenes or imagine scenes as old, posed photographs viewed from a distance; in the look condition they viewed pictures without controlling their responses.
